line_items.reasoning: Q1-2024 NII ex-Markets was revised up slightly to ~$89B (from the prior $88B guide), and total revenue of $42.5B annualizes well above the ~$90B total NII guide, with IB fees surging 21% YoY and First Republic contributing above-plan revenue, all pointing to a clear beat vs. the conservative Q4-2023 revenue guidance.
ROTCE came in at 21% in Q1-2024, materially above the guided normalization toward ~17% through-the-cycle, though card net charge-offs are rising and deposit margin compression continues as guided.
Card net charge-offs rose $825M YoY with a reserve build expected in the back half of 2024, suggesting the card NCO rate is tracking above the guided <3.5% ceiling for full-year 2024.
Q1-2024 expenses came in at $22B (up 9% YoY), driven in part by a $725M incremental FDIC special assessment, putting the annualized run rate above the ~$90B full-year adjusted expense guide.
Buybacks remained at ~$2B/quarter as guided, with the pace unchanged pending Basel III end-game and SCB clarity, exactly in line with prior guidance.
